messages:
kevin_support: Hey team — customer reporting intermittent 401s for /v1/generate. They supplied request_id 8f3c2a9b. Can someone pull server logs for that req id and confirm whether it was an auth failure upstream or token mismatch?

ingrid_sre: On it. Quick question — is the request coming from hosted API or Dedicated?

kevin_support: Hosted API (region: us-west-2). Customer said it happens ~1 in 200 requests, no pattern.

maria_support: Also they attached a sample curl, copying here:```curl -v \n -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-REDACTED" \n -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"test"}' \n https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```

logs-bot: Searching logs for request_id:8f3c2a9b ... found 1 matching trace in prod-usw2-frontend (ts: 2026-05-22T14:12:03Z). Pulling full trace. :mag: 

logs-bot: Trace snippet: ```auth.check: token_valid=false reason=expired_token user_id=null
upstream: auth_proxy.rs: token_lookup=cache_miss
response: 401 Unauthorized x-server-request-id=8f3c2a9b
```

ingrid_sre: Hmm looks like the token was expired on that hit. Can we check if there's any clock skew or token refresh failures from the client? Also verify our auth proxy logs around that time for repeated failures from same client IP.

kevin_support: Asked customer for client SDK version and whether they use long-lived tokens. They replied they use our JS SDK v1.4.2 and refresh flow via auth server.

maria_support: While we're at it can we confirm retention window? Customer's legal requested logs from 2026-02-10 which we might have archived.

logs-bot: Logs TTL for prod-usw2: 90 days hot storage, 365 days cold archive (S3). Direct queries only cover hot storage. Archive access requires support bundle or S3 retrieval request. The 2026-02-10 window is archived; we can request retrieval (ETA ~3–6 hours).

ingrid_sre: For immediate triage, we have the live trace for the req id. Also running a quick Kibana-style query to catch nearby hits: `request_id:8f3c2a9b OR request_meta.client_ip:203.0.113.45 OR user_agent:"redwood-js/1.4.2"`

ingrid_sre: Found 6 attempts from same IP within 60s; three were 401, then a 200. Looks like occasional token expiry before refresh completed. Suggest we ask customer to increase refresh retry/backoff and confirm SDK is invoking refresh before expiry.

kevin_support: Noted. I asked them to update to SDK 1.5.0 (contains pre-refresh fix). Also requested a debug bundle in case more traces are needed. Included instructions: `redwoodctl support bundle create --req 8f3c2a9b --include-logs --expires 7d`

maria_support: Customer asks how to provide a curl reproduction showing the issue. Suggested steps: 1) record exact Authorization header value and timestamps 2) reproduce with same system clock (or record `date -u`) 3) capture response headers including `Date` and `x-server-request-id`. Example curl:```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Date: $(date -u)" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate```

ingrid_sre: We'll keep monitoring and can escalate to auth team if we see token signing errors. For now, root cause = token expiry race during refresh. If they want historical logs from Feb 10, we can submit an archive retrieval — confirm with legal and I'll kick off the S3 retrieval.

kevin_support: Thanks all. I pinged the customer with SDK upgrade + repro steps + debug bundle command. Keeping this thread open until we get either the debug bundle or confirmation that upgrade fixed it. :white_check_mark:
